scores.evidence: Yjs garbage collection removes deleted content, so the log is the only source for full history.
scores.rationale: Claims about CRDT convergence, state-vector resync, Y.RelativePosition anchors, local-only UndoManager and confirm-after-commit durability are all accurate, including subtle areas like GC vs history.

scores.evidence: Full offline-first editing (days offline, conflict review UI). Pull forward when a mobile app is planned
scores.rationale: Covers every core capability of real-time co-editing, resolves ambiguities with stated defaults, and every exclusion is explicit with a pull-forward trigger.

scores.evidence: The log is proven to be the source of truth, so any node can rebuild any document.
scores.rationale: Single source of truth, data ownership, consistency model and routing decisions are honored consistently across phases with no contradictions; presence, history and permissions all follow the stated gates.

scores.evidence: fuzz suite runs 10,000 random multi-client edit sequences with... server kills mid-commit. Every confirmed update survives
scores.rationale: Validation targets the exact domain risks (divergence, durability, failover) with seeded reproducible tests, checkable per-phase exit criteria, a Phase-0 prod proof, and a production divergence detector.

scores.evidence: Storage cost passes budget (e.g. more than $X per workspace per month).
scores.rationale: Design-critical assumptions and revisit triggers are explicit and numbers are mostly flagged as examples, but some targets (16 ms, 99.5%) and team/scale baselines appear without stated basis.

scores.evidence: If a client's hash differs from the server's at the same state vector, the client is forced to resync and an alert fires.
scores.rationale: Covers the hardest domain failures—silent divergence, duplicates, node death mid-commit, malformed/malicious input, revocation on live sockets—each with concrete detection, containment and recovery.

scores.evidence: Graceful drain on deploy. Stop accepting connections, hand off documents, then close sockets with a reconnect hint.
scores.rationale: Deployment, migrations, meaningful alerts and drain/failover are concrete and team-sized, but explicit rollback procedure and incident ownership/on-call are not stated.

scores.evidence: or if its memory per document exceeds budget (more than ~50 MB for a 1 MB document)
scores.rationale: Identifies the real cost drivers (log storage growth, per-document memory, build-vs-buy) with concrete controls and gates, though no order-of-magnitude dollar or people-cost estimates are given.

scores.evidence: the costliest to reverse, because the stored document format follows it... Decide before Phase 1 ends.
scores.rationale: Explicitly ranks the CRDT/stored-format choice as the one-way door, deadlines its revisit, defers plugin API until the schema stabilizes, and gives triggers and migration consequences for every major decision.

scores.evidence: One codebase, two process roles... Split further only when one area needs its own scaling or release cadence.
scores.rationale: Starts with the simplest workable design (monolith, single sync node, buy identity/storage), gates every added complexity behind measured triggers, and omits nothing essential.

scores.evidence: User A opens `/d/<id>` and types "hello". User B, in another browser, sees "hello" in under 500 ms.
scores.rationale: Dependency-justified phase ordering, specific technology and schema decisions, concrete first slice, and checkable exit criteria per phase mean a team could start immediately.

traps.evidence: Adopt: Yjs, y-protocols, ProseMirror/Tiptap, Hocuspocus as the sync-server base.

The server confirms an update only after it is durably committed to Postgres. "Saved" means committed.

note: An exemplary plan: proven CRDT library, durable confirm-after-commit, convergence fuzzing and divergence detection built first, with every deferral gated; only rich-text merge semantics detail, rollback/ownership, and dollar-level cost grounding fall short.
